analysis.title: Weekly Warm-up: Buy the Rumor, Sell the News
key_insights: MS US equity strategy says the correction that began in June is entering its final phase as the S&P 500 catches down to narrow breadth and approaches the 7100-7300 downside range, which has valuation, trendline and retracement support.

A retest of last week's lows, possibly a temporary break, is expected over the coming week(s) and is described as setting up a year-end rally. MS recommends adding exposure over the next few weeks rather than waiting for a perfect low.
MS recommends adding quality cyclicals that have de-rated materially and show strong EPS revisions. Industrials stay attractive on an equal-weight basis into next year.

The SOX is down about 40% since June and is tracking MS's silver-stock analog of a parabolic blow-off and aftermath. MS turned negative on Semis in June when revisions breadth for the industry peaked, and now thinks the group is in a bottoming process that may need a retest.

MS says the economy and earnings cycle moved from early-cycle to mid-cycle, driven by the peak rate of change in EPS revisions breadth and a shift to more hawkish monetary policy under a new Fed chair. Quality has materially outperformed since the rotation call.

MS's capex mapping shows 2027 data center capex is about 5% of S&P 500 consensus revenue, and the 2028 share is slightly higher but still mid-single-digit. Even if some capacity is pushed out, the impact on S&P 500 revenue and earnings is limited and priced at 18x forward earnings, near Liberation Day valuation levels.

The case for a retest rests on positioning and technicals, including leveraged ETF and macro systematic supply flagged by the QDS team and a possible final spike in correlation. The sentiment/positioning indicator fell last week but is not yet at March selloff levels.
Equity vol spiked last week to catch up with bond vol, which MS reads as a sign of a bottom forming. The Headline Global Risk Demand Index is close to the extreme reading that marks a low.

The wildcard is a Fed that stays more hawkish than expected, which would make the bottoming process longer and bleed into December. MS compares this to 2018, Powell's first year as chair, with Warsh in the same position now and facing a more hawkish FOMC.

Possible midterm positives: oil has fallen sharply on White House comments read as a sign an Iran deal could come together (still uncertain), a possible reversal of SNAP and Medicaid cuts, and a possible pull-forward of business activity and M&A before the 2028 election. Markets typically trade poorly into midterms and well in the 6-12 months after.
The SPX vs breadth spread has converged to 2%, which MS reads as a sign the correction is in its final stages.

MS thematic research, using an LLM on about 18,000 transcripts, finds 44% of S&P 500 companies cited a quantifiable AI benefit over the trailing 12 months, up from 32% a year ago. Market-cap weighted the figure is 54% versus 53%. The share citing financial impact rose to 26% from 16%.

AI adopters that frequently discuss quantifiable benefits show faster NTM EPS growth than the S&P 500 on a sector-neutral basis. About 22% of S&P 500 companies cited an AI cost, up from about 8%, with token, inference and API costs now the dominant category.

Financials is furthest along on AI quantification: 67% of Financials companies cited AI benefits, up from 42%, and 46% cited AI costs, up from 14%. Communication Services (61%) and Information Technology (51%) follow.

Q3 2026 earnings season: median T+1 price reaction is 0.0% absolute and +0.5% relative. EPS surprise is 3.9% versus a 4.4% historical average, and sales surprise is 2.4-2.5% versus a 1.3% average. Blended Q3 EPS growth is 33.5% Y/Y on sales growth of 13.5%.

Calendar 2026 and 2027 EPS growth is 33% and 16%. For 2027, the S&P 493 is expected to grow earnings faster than the Mag 7 (16% vs 12%), mostly on difficult Mag 7 comps from one-off non-operating gains.
S&P 500 earnings are being skewed by unrealized gains on private AI investments, which inflated Q1 and Q2 growth and affect forward growth rates.
Earnings revisions breadth is +10% and has not rebounded as strongly in Q3, which suggests upward revisions to 2027 slowed. FCF surprise separates winners from losers more than EPS surprise in Q3.
Q3 consensus margins are 15.7% for the S&P 500, with LTM EBIT margin at 20.2% and expected at 22.7% for FY2027. Semis EBIT margin is expected at 59.9% for 2027.

MS analysts' systematic previews were net +20% on KPI and +22% on NTM EPS, versus +32% and +27% last quarter. Post-report NTM EPS revisions across MS coverage are net +15% versus +27% last quarter, with Tech (+43%) and Real Estate (+33%) strongest.
MS Fresh Money Buy List has ten names. The current list averages a 19.5% total return since inclusion with an average hold of 23.3 months.
MS strategy forecast table: S&P 500 at 7,377 with a base-case 12-month target of 8,300 (+13%), a bull case of 9,400 (+27%) and a bear case of 5,900 (-20%). Current P/E is 17.7x.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 blended EPS growth is 33.5% Y/Y (FactSet, 436 of 495 companies reported) on sales growth of 13.5% Y/Y. Sales surprise is 2.5% versus a 1.3% historical average.
Q3 2026 EPS surprise is 3.9% reported versus a 4.4% historical average, well below the Q2 2026 EPS surprise of +26%, which non-operating profits from private AI investments skewed.

Median T+1 price reaction to Q3 reports is 0.0% absolute and +0.5% relative, with 49% of reactions positive. Companies need to beat on both EPS and FCF for strong T+1 gains, and FCF surprise separates winners from losers more than EPS surprise.
Consensus expects calendar 2026 EPS growth of 33% and 2027 growth of 16% (consensus estimates). Mag 7 earnings are expected to grow 26% in Q3 2026 versus 23% for the S&P 493 (estimates).
For 2027 consensus has the S&P 493 growing 16% versus 12% for the Mag 7, largely on difficult Mag 7 comps from one-off non-operating gains.

MS systematic results across US coverage show net +15% NTM EPS revisions after Q3 reports versus +30% (+27% in another passage) after Q2. Tech is +43% and Real Estate +33%. Materials (-3%) and Communication Services (-5%) are slightly negative.
Semiconductors reported Q3 EPS growth of 253.7% Y/Y with a 6.1% surprise. Information Technology contributes 13.5 points of the 33.5% S&P 500 EPS growth.

trade_ideas.description: Add exposure to quality cyclicals that have de-rated materially and show strong EPS revisions, building positions over the next few weeks as the S&P 500 tests 7100-7300.
trade_ideas.rationale: The correction is in its final phase, a retest should set up a year-end rally, and quality cyclicals have de-rated while their EPS revisions stay strong.
trade_ideas.risk: A Fed that stays more hawkish than expected could extend the bottoming process into December.

trade_ideas.rationale: AI adoption fits the quality rotation and is MS's highest-conviction theme into 2027.

risk_factors: A Fed that stays more hawkish than expected (Chair Warsh facing a hawkish FOMC) could lengthen the bottoming process into December.
The retest could bring a temporary break of last week's lows, with a final spike in correlation and supply from leveraged ETFs and systematic macro funds.
Data center capex could be pushed out beyond the 2027-2028 horizon, though MS sees limited impact on S&P 500 revenue and earnings.
The sentiment indicator has not reached the March selloff lows, so capitulation may be incomplete.
S&P 500 earnings growth is inflated by unrealized gains on private AI investments, and weak upward revisions to 2027 suggest slowing momentum.
Rising AI-related costs, mainly token, inference and API usage, keep total AI spend in focus.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P 500 is close to the 7100-7300 support range, breadth is catching up with the index, equity vol has caught up to bond vol, and the GRDI is near buy levels. A retest on lower momentum should mark the low and resolve into a year-end rally.
tension_points.bear_case: The sentiment indicator is not yet at March or 2018 lows, leveraged ETF and systematic supply may persist, and a hawkish Fed under Chair Warsh could tighten financial conditions as it did in late 2018 and extend the bottoming process into December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed that remains more hawkish than expected, which leads to a more drawn out bottoming process that bleeds into December.

tension_points.bull_case: Data center capex is only 5% of 2027 consensus S&P 500 revenue and mid-single-digit in 2028, so even a delay has limited impact, and the market already prices it at 18x forward earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Midterm policy uncertainty could push a portion of data center capacity beyond the 2027-2028 horizon, and Semis and other data center beneficiaries have already underperformed materially.
